rationale: itnet_v3-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=0.0001, epochs=9, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=460, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=820, seed=42, rationale=iter-7 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). BASE_ITER=5 (the BEST: c16/ep9/train_n=400, hr 0.328842). ONE KNOB: train_n 400 -> 460 (MIDDLE coverage) at FIXED epochs=9 -- i.e. raise data coverage while HOLDING per-slice exposure at the proven 9x level. This is the clean single-knob test iter-6 could NOT run: iter-6 funded FULL data (tn579) by CUTTING epochs to 6 (parity), so it lost on BOTH axes vs iter-5 (grad_steps 3474<3600 AND exposure 6x<9x) and REGRESSED to hr 0.315239. iter-7 instead adds coverage at constant exposure. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) itnet_v3 trajectory: iter-1 ep8/tn200 hr 0.268409 (737.85s); iter-2 ep14/tn200 hr 0.310054 (1010.07s); iter-3 ep18/tn200 hr 0.312282 (1072.94s, epochs PLATEAUED); iter-4 ep9/c24/tn200 hr 0.295576 (834.0s, capacity REGRESSED -> revert c16); iter-5 BEST ep9/c16/tn400 hr 0.328842 / SSIM 0.915763 / PSNR 37.54 / RMSE 0.000664 (1006.81s=16.78min, 193s budget UNSPENT); iter-6 ep6/c16/tn579 hr 0.315239 / SSIM 0.906478 (914.0s=15.2min, 286s budget UNSPENT). PER-EPOCH COST scales LINEARLY with train_n (bs=1, 0.1723 s/slice): tn400->68.9s/ep, tn460->79.3s/ep, tn579->99.7s/ep. So at the 1200s wall full data (tn579) can only buy ep6-7 (<=7x exposure) while tn400 buys ep9-10 (9-10x). (2) LIMITER: the EPOCHS-vs-DATA tradeoff at the budget. iter-6 proved FULL data UNDER-TRAINS in-budget: tn579 only affords ep6 = 6x exposure, worse than tn400/ep9 = 9x. The per-epoch cost of the last 30% of data is too high to keep exposure at 9x. itnet_v3 needs ~9x exposure to converge in-budget (epochs plateaued only at ep18 on tn200; ep6 is clearly under-trained). So coverage is only worth raising IF exposure stays >=9x. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 400 -> 460, epochs HELD at 9 (NOT cut). This is the LARGEST train_n that still affords ep9 inside the wall: 481 fixed + 9*460*0.1723 = 1194s = 19.9 min < 1200s (and the model OVER-predicts by 95-165s -- iter-6 landed 165s under -- so real elapsed ~1060s/17.7min). It beats iter-5 on coverage (69%->79%) AND grad_steps (3600->4140) at IDENTICAL 9x exposure; it beats iter-6 on exposure (6x->9x) and grad_steps (3474->4140). tn480+ would force ep8 (8x exposure, below the proven 9x) so 460 is the sweet spot: max coverage at >=9x exposure. (4) HYPOTHESIS: adding 60 distinct training slices (400->460, 69%->79% coverage) WHILE HOLDING exposure at 9x lifts hr above the iter-5 best 0.328842, because iter-6 showed the data lever works ONLY when exposure is not sacrificed -- and here it is not. NUMERIC FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.3288 at tn460/ep9, itnet_v3 is at its budget-constrained ceiling (~0.329, the tn400/ep9 point) -- it cannot afford enough epochs on more data, and even coverage-at-constant-exposure does not help -> file the ceiling, stays #3. (5) BUDGET (HARD 1200s = train+score): fixed 481s, per_slice 0.1723s; epochs=(1200-481)/(460*0.1723)=9.07 -> ep9 is the max integer that fits. total=481+9*460*0.1723=1194s conservative (real ~1060s). Train-only=9*460*0.1723=713s < max_train_s=820 backstop, so it never truncates (checks between epochs; fences only runaway slowdown); the 214-slice per-sample val + figure always land inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside dc_step overflows otherwise). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-sample itnet.projector swap for the k=3 DC steps, bg_target=truth. (6) do NOT return control mid-campaign. Predicted iter-7 hr: 0.33-0.34 if coverage-at-9x-exposure helps; <=0.3288 falsifies -> budget-constrained ceiling at ~0.329, stays #3.
